Subject: Quick: OneTrust connector + CAIQ fragments for procurement

Hi Monica and Marcus,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement at BrightWave needs us live in OneTrust to accept CAIQ fragments and an S3 staging area for evidence. Two asks from their side:

1) Can Redwood provide a service-account S3 bucket or presigned upload workflow (they prefer presigned URLs) so we can drop SOC 2 artifacts and CAIQ fragment PDFs?
2) They want a mapping matrix that shows which Redwood controls map to CAIQ questions (we can accept a fragment-level CSV).

Attached is a short list of the fragments they want prioritized and an internal procurement SLA (BrightWave_CAIQ_Fragment_Request.pdf). Our legal team will also need the onboarding contact for any contract redlines.

Can you confirm an estimated timeline and whether IP allowlisting or a service account is required?

Thanks,
Rajesh Patel
Head of Vendor Risk
BrightWave Inc.

Attachments: BrightWave_CAIQ_Fragment_Request.pdf
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: OneTrust connector + CAIQ fragments for procurement

Hi Rajesh —

Appreciate the clear asks. High-level answers:

- We can support S3 presigned uploads into a temporary ingestion bucket. Our security team prefers presigned URLs for short-lived uploads; we will create a manifest and a single-use presigned URL package.
- For mapping, we have an export that maps Redwood security controls to CAIQ identifiers. I can produce a fragment CSV for your prioritized items (we'll mark which controls are SOC2-scoped).
- IP allowlisting is optional for presigned flows but required if you want long-lived service accounts or SFTP.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus will scope SOC2-in-scope controls and hand back the CAIQ fragment CSV.
2) Karthik will confirm the presigned URL TTL, upload manifest format, and whether we need a temporary access window.
3) I'll coordinate onboarding docs and drop the OneTrust connector instructions (redwood_onetrust-connector-instructions.md).

If that sounds good, we'll aim to deliver the CSV + presigned manifest by EOD Monday (2026-12-13).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Partner Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: security@brightwave.com, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: OneTrust connector + CAIQ fragments for procurement

Rajesh —

Technical details:
- Presigned workflow: We'll generate a manifest (s3-presigned-upload-manifest.csv) with expected file names and checksums. Each manifest entry gets a presigned PUT URL valid for 48 hours (TTL: 172800s).
- OneTrust ingestion: Onetrust will pull artifacts if we expose an authenticated endpoint; otherwise we can push artifacts into a shared OneTrust S3 connector. Onetrust team (cc'd in original) can confirm connector configuration.
- Authentication & IPs: For the 48h presigned flow, no IP allowlist required. For a persistent service account or SFTP, you must provide IP ranges to whitelist and a dedicated service account key.

Operational asks from BrightWave:
1) Which artifacts will be included per CAIQ fragment (pdf + evidence manifest)?
2) Do you want an automated daily ingest for any rolling evidence, or a one-time bulk upload?

I'll stand up the presign package and drop the manifest to Monica once we confirm bulk vs rolling.

—Karthik Iyer
Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference

I'll upload the initial fragment PDFs to the presign package once Monica publishes it.
